chapter: Return to Chicago: the Blue Note and Rupneck's
title: Following the Red Allen band in Minneapolis
summary: Williamson books Hodes solo in Minneapolis after Red Allen's band. Hodes finds he cannot compete in sound.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: No, in Chicago. And John Skenk was there and said, we got togetherness, and we wanted to book me and manage me. And we set that up. And I thought, well, looks to me that there could be work here. Freddie Williamson gave me two weeks in Minneapolis at a bar behind the bar. And the boss is running around for three days, moving the microphones while I'm playing.
And finally, it dawns on me. Who am I following? He says, Red Allen. I says, you can move mikes from now til Doomsday, you're never going to get me sounding like that band.
Solo, following the Red Allen band, the loudest jazz band I've ever heard.
For a small group. And I'm following him,
